entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12803"/><div sID="gen23777" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12803"/><hi type="bold">5. Trust ye not in a friend--</hi>Faith is kept nowhere: all to a man are treacherous (<reference osisRef="Jer.9.2-Jer.9.6">Jr 9:2-6</reference>). When justice is perverted by the great, faith nowhere is safe. So, in gospel times of persecution, "a man's foes are they of his own household" (<reference osisRef="Matt.10.35">Mt 10:35</reference>, <reference osisRef="Matt.10.36">36</reference>; <reference osisRef="Luke.12.53">Lu 12:53</reference>).<div eID="gen23777" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23778" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">guide--</hi>a counsellor [Calvin] able to help and advise (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.118.8">Psa 118:8</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.118.9">9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.146.3">146:3</reference>). The head of your family, to whom all the members of the family would naturally repair in emergencies. Similarly the Hebrew is translated in <reference osisRef="Josh.22.14">Jos 22:14</reference> and "chief friends" in <reference osisRef="Prov.16.28">Pr 16:28</reference> [Grotius].<div eID="gen23778" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23779" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">her that lieth in thy bosom--</hi>thy wife (<reference osisRef="Deut.13.6">De 13:6</reference>). <div eID="gen23779" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12805"/><div sID="gen23781" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12805"/><hi type="bold">7. Therefore I will look unto the Lord--</hi>as if no one else were before mine eyes. We must not only "look unto the Lord," but also "wait for Him." Having no hope from man (<reference osisRef="Mic.7.5">Mi 7:5</reference>, <reference osisRef="Mic.7.6">6</reference>), Micah speaks in the name of Israel, who herein, taught by chastisement (<reference osisRef="Mic.7.4">Mi 7:4</reference>) to feel her sin (<reference osisRef="Mic.7.9">Mi 7:9</reference>), casts herself on the Lord as her only hope," in patient waiting (<reference osisRef="Lam.3.26">La 3:26</reference>). She did so under the Babylonian captivity; she shall do so again hereafter when the spirit of grace shall be poured on her (<reference osisRef="Zech.12.10-Zech.12.13">Zec 12:10-13</reference>). <div eID="gen23781" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_plain: 9. bear-- patiently. the indignation of the Lord-- His punishment inflicted on me ( La 3:39 ). The true penitent "accepts the punishment of his iniquity" ( Le 26:41 , 43 ); they who murmur against God, do not yet know their guilt ( Job 40:4 , 5 ). execute judgment for me-- against my foe. God's people plead guilty before God; but, in respect to their human foes, they are innocent and undeserving of their foes' injuries. bring me forth to the light-- to the temporal and spiritual redemption. I shall behold his righteousness-- His gracious faithfulness to His promises ( Psa 103:17 ).

In that day also--</hi>rather, an answer to the supposed question of Zion, When shall my walls be built? "The day (of thy walls being built) is the day when he (that is, many) shall come to thee from Assyria," &c. [Ludovicus De Dieu]. The Assyrians (including the Babylonians) who spoiled thee shall come.<div eID="gen23796" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23797" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">and from the fortified cities--</hi>rather, to suit the parallelism, "from Assyria even to Egypt." (Matzor may be so translated). So Assyria and Egypt are contrasted in <reference osisRef="Isa.19.23">Is 19:23</reference> [Maurer]. Calvin agrees with English Version, "from all fortified cities."<div eID="gen23797" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23798" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">from the fortress even to the river--</hi>"from Egypt even to the river" Euphrates (answering in parallelism to "Assyria") [Maurer]. Compare <reference osisRef="Isa.11.15">Is 11:15</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.11.16">16</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.19.23-Isa.19.25">19:23-25</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.27.13">27:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hos.11.11">Ho 11:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.10.10">Zec 10:10</reference>. <div eID="gen23798" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 12. In that day also-- rather, an answer to the supposed question of Zion, When shall my walls be built? "The day (of thy walls being built) is the day when he (that is, many) shall come to thee from Assyria," &c. [Ludovicus De Dieu]. The Assyrians (including the Babylonians) who spoiled thee shall come. and from the fortified cities-- rather, to suit the parallelism, "from Assyria even to Egypt." (Matzor may be so translated). So Assyria and Egypt are contrasted in Is 19:23 [Maurer]. Abraham--</hi>Thou shalt make good to their posterity the promise made to the patriarchs. God's promises are called "mercy," because they flow slowly from grace; "truth," because they will be surely performed (<reference osisRef="Luke.1.72">Lu 1:72</reference>, 73; <reference osisRef="1Thess.5.24">1Th 5:24</reference>).<div eID="gen23825" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23826" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">sworn unto our fathers--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Ps.105.9">Psa 105:9</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.105.10">10</reference>). This unchangeable promise implied an engagement that the seed of the patriarchs should never perish, and should be restored to their inheritance as often as they turned wholly to God (<reference osisRef="Deut.30.1">De 30:1</reference>, 2). <chapter eID="Mic.7"/><div eID="gen23826" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen23519" osisID="Mic" type="book"/>
